repositories.readme:
# Chronicles of the Realm · 江山时序

English · 简体中文 (Chinese) · 繁體中文 (Traditional Chinese) · 日本語 (Japanese)

**An Interactive Historical Atlas of China from the Warring States (403 BCE) to the Present — Scrub Through Time, Trace Ancient Cities, and Walk in the Footsteps of History** [**Play Live Demo (English UI) → https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en**](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en) *The story behind it (in Chinese): [From textbook maps to 1k GitHub stars](https://deanchen.me/history/atlas/2026/10/25/jiangshan-map-story.html)*

--- ## Why It's Fun to Explore Have you ever wondered while reading Chinese history or classical poetry: - *"Where exactly on today's map are Jiankang (the Six Dynasties capital), Huangzhou (where Su Dongpo composed the Red Cliffs Rhapsody in exile), Languan Pass in the Qinling Mountains (where Han Yu halted his horse in the snow), or Zhuxianzhen (Yue Fei's northern campaign frontier)?"* - *"How many names did Chang'an hold across two millennia, and what pivotal events unfolded on that soil?"* - *"How did the realm evolve step by step—from the Partition of Jin and the Seven Warring States at the opening of Sima Guang's Zizhi Tongjian (403 BCE), Qin's unification campaigns, Emperor Wu of Han opening the Hexi Corridor, High Tang's Four Garrisons of Anxi, and Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan jurisdiction over Tibet, to Zeng Jize's recovery of Ili (1881 CE) and the 20th-century shift from the 'Begonia Leaf' (秋海棠) map to the 'Rooster' (雄鸡) map?"* **Chronicles of the Realm (`jiangshan-map`)** brings together **2,400+ years** of Chinese history across **18 historical periods** into a single interactive parchment atlas—featuring **multi-stage territorial and prefecture snapshots**, **ancient cities**, **strategic mountain passes**, **poetic and battlefield landmarks**, **chronological milestones**, and **reigning monarchs & imperial eras**. No heavy print atlases required—just drag the timeline and click any city to travel through space and time. --- ### Feature 1: Scrub the Timeline to Watch Realms Rise & Fall, Track Monarchs, and Compare Ancient & Modern Borders - **Multi-Polity Confrontations on a Single Canvas**: From the Seven Warring States (Qin, Chu, Qi, Yan, Zhao, Wei, Han) alongside Zhou, Yue, Ba-Shu, Zhongshan, and Yiqu, to the Three Kingdoms warlords (Yuan Shao, Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Sun Quan, Gongsun's Liaodong), Northern & Southern Dynasties, Five Dynasties & Ten Kingdoms, and Song, Liao, Western Xia, Dali, Jin, and the Mongols—all rendered side-by-side in high-contrast traditional parchment hues. Hover over any polity in the bottom-left legend to highlight its territory, or click to zoom straight to it. - **Multi-Stage Territorial Evolution & Dashed "Ghost Boundary Diffs"**: At every major territorial milestone—such as Qin's conquest of Ba-Shu (316 BCE), Yan General Qin Kai's expansion into Liaodong (300 BCE), Ma Yuan's bronze pillars in Jiaozhi (43 CE), Sima Yi's campaign in Liaodong (238 CE), Li Jing's conquest of Tuyuhun (635 CE), the Four Garrisons of Anxi & Wang Xuance's campaign in Central India (648 CE), Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan rule over Tibet (1288 CE), Ming's Hami & Seven Guards West of Jiayuguan (1404 CE), the 1881 Treaty of Saint Petersburg recovering Ili, the 1898 foreign leased territories, the 1945 retrocession of Taiwan, and the 1946 transition from the **"Begonia Leaf" (秋海棠)** map to the **"Rooster" (雄鸡)** map—click any milestone or phase dot to switch maps and reveal the previous phase's dashed vermilion **Ghost Boundary Diff** so territorial gains and losses are immediately visible. - **Inline Reigning Monarch & Imperial Era Display**: The timeline dynamically displays the reigning monarch (temple/posthumous title + personal name + reign span, e.g., `Emperor Wu of Han · Liu Che`, `Emperor Taizong of Tang · Li Shimin`, `Emperor Shengzu of Qing · Xuanye`) alongside the exact imperial era year. - **Ancient Prefecture Hover Inspection & Modern X-Ray Lens**: First-level administrative divisions (Commanderies, Circuits, Routes, and Provinces) are rendered with deduplicated **Parchment Casing** borders. Zoom in and hover over any prefecture (e.g., Ming `Yingtian Prefecture` or Three Kingdoms `Jingzhou`) to inspect its jurisdiction and modern provincial equivalents, or toggle the **X-Ray Lens** to project modern provincial boundaries directly over the historical map. - **Dynamic River Courses, Ancient Lakes & Grand Engineering Works**: As you scrub through time, historical shifts of the Yellow River, expanding and shrinking ancient lakes (*Yunmeng Marsh*, *Lop Nur / Puchanghai*), Warring States/Qin/Han/Ming Great Walls, Sui-Tang & Grand Canals, the Silk Road, and Zheng He's maritime routes evolve in lockstep with each era; ancient coastlines around the Bohai Gulf, northern Jiangsu, the Yangtze estuary, and the Pearl River Delta also advance and retreat by era. - **Zoomable Timeline**: Drag the handles at either end of the timeline inward to zoom into one stretch of history (handy for short eras such as Qin, the Three Kingdoms, or the Five Dynasties); double-click the timeline to return to the full overview. > [Try It Live: Ming Dynasty Yongle 13 (1415 CE) · Two Capitals, Thirteen Provinces & "Yingtian Prefecture" Inspection →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1415&zoom=1.75¢er=115.8,33.2&hover=Yingtian%20Prefecture&lang=en) ![Ming Dynasty 1415 CE · Yingtian Prefecture Hover Preview](assets/preview_1415_ming_yingtian_en.webp) --- ### Feature 2: Click Any Ancient City or Strategic Pass to Uncover 2,400 Years of History (`Trace Place`) **Click any ancient city or mountain pass** on the map (or double-click anywhere on the canvas) to open its **Trace Place** genealogy card: - **Bilingual City Lore Banner & 2,400-Year Administrative Genealogy**: At the top of the card, read a curated **poetic epigraph and historical biography** for the city; below, trace how its name and administrative jurisdiction evolved across all 18 historical eras—from Warring States and Qin commanderies, Han regional inspectorates, Tang circuits, and Song routes to Yuan/Ming/Qing provinces and modern municipalities—complete with `Imperial Capital` badges and dynastic seat remarks. - **Site-Specific Landmark Events**: Beneath each dynasty row, inspect major historical events that took place right on that spot (e.g., *Shang Yang's Reforms* and *Qin's Unification* at Xianyang, *Guan Yu Flooding the Seven Armies* at Fancheng, the *Xuanwu Gate Incident* at Chang'an, or *Yue Fei's Martyrdom* at Lin'an). Click the **`Key Events`** pill in the top-right of the card to filter for dynasties with major events, and click any event to time-travel straight to that year! - **Strategic Mountain Passes & Poetic / Battlefield Landmarks**: Explore famous mountain passes—including *Hangu Pass*, *Tongguan*, *Jianmen Pass*, *Yanmen Pass*, *Yumen Pass*, *Yangguan*, and *Shanhai Pass*—rendered with traditional *Hanque* gatehouse icons and strategic terrain notes, alongside famous battlefields and literary landmarks such as *Red Cliffs (Chibi)*, *Gaixia*, *Wuzhang Plains*, *Orchid Pavilion (Lanting)*, *Yueyang Tower*, *Pavilion of Prince Teng*, *Languan Pass*, *Loulan*, *Lop Nur*, and *Issyk-Kul*. > [Try It Live: High Tang Kaiyuan 29 (741 CE) · Open Chang'an's 2,400-Year Genealogy Card →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=741&place=Chang'an&lang=en) ![High Tang 741 CE · Chang'an Trace Place & Key Events](assets/preview_741_tang_trace_en.webp) --- ### Feature 3: Person Chronicles — Trace Any Historical Figure Across Time & Space Click the top-left **Universal Search Box** (with a rotatable `e.g.` figure preview and quick-search chips, or type any monarch, general, statesman, monk, or poet such as `Cao Cao`, `Huo Qubing`, `Sima Qian`, `Yue Fei`, or `Zheng He`) to open **Person Chronicle (`点人溯事`)**, plotting every milestone of their life with delicate cartographic hairline arcs and directional ticks across changing dynastic borders: - **Qin Shi Huang's Unification Campaigns (238–221 BCE)**: From suppressing the rebellion at Xianyang and Wang Jian's attack on Ye, to the fall of Han, Zhao, Yan, Wei, Chu, and Dai, culminating in the surrender of Qi at Linzi—as you advance stop by stop, watch the six rival kingdoms merge into the Qin Empire right on the map! - **Zhang Qian's Mission to the Western Regions (138–126 BCE)**: Depart Chang'an, endure over a decade of Xiongnu captivity without surrendering the Han imperial staff, and blaze the trail to Dayuan (Fergana), Kangju, and the Greater Yuezhi. - **Zhuge Liang's Emergence & Northern Expeditions (207–234 CE)**: From the Three Visits at Longzhong and the alliance at Chaisang before Red Cliffs, to entering Shu, the White Emperor City entrustment, the Southern Campaign across the Lu River, Hanzhong's *Memorial on Deploying the Troops*, Mount Qi, and the autumn winds of Wuzhang Plains. - **Xuanzang's Pilgrimage to India (627–645 CE)**: Slip past Yumen Pass alone across the Moheyan Desert, scale the icy Bedel Pass, cross the Indus, study at Nalanda Monastery, and debate at Kanyakubja (Kanauj) before returning to Chang'an. - **Li Bai's Grand Travels Across Tang China (701–762 CE)**: From Suyab and boyhood in Shu, sailing out through the Three Gorges at twenty-four, scattering gold in Yangzhou, serving in the Hanlin Academy at Chang'an, meeting Du Fu in Luoyang, receiving amnesty at White Emperor City, to his final years at Dangtu. - **Su Shi's Literary Exile Across Song China (1056–1101 CE)**: From leaving Meishan for the capital Kaifeng and gazing at the moon in Mizhou, to composing the *Red Cliffs Rhapsody* in Huangzhou exile, Huizhou, and crossing the sea to Danzhou on Hainan Island. - **Wang Yangming's Unity of Knowledge & Action (1472–1529 CE)**: From birth in Yuyao and imprisonment in Beijing, to his enlightenment at Longchang in Guizhou, pacifying bandits in Southern Ganzhou, capturing the rebel Prince of Ning in 35 days, teaching at the Tianquan Bridge in Shaoxing, and his final words *"This mind is bright and clear; what more is there to say?"* at Nan'an. - **Multi-Person Chronicles**: Type two or three names into the search box (e.g. `Li Bai, Du Fu, Gao Shi` or `Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Sun Quan`) to merge their journeys onto one timeline. Places where they met in the same year are marked as shared encounters, and the `Shared N` pill narrows the list to just those stops. - **Event Storylines**: Major events unfold stop by stop, just like a person's life. The An Lushan Rebellion (755–763 CE) is laid out in ten stops across three acts, with the Tang loyalists and the rebels drawn in two colors so each side's advances are easy to follow. Each time you step to the next event (`‹ / ›`, `← / →`, or `Space` to auto-play), **the timeline year, reigning monarch, imperial era, and dynastic territories evolve in sync with their footsteps**, highlighting the active transition arc alongside bilingual primary-source excerpts and poems written at that exact site. > [Try It Live: Follow Su Dongpo's Exile to Mizhou & Huangzhou (1075–1082 CE) →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=sushi&lang=en) ![Person Chronicle · Su Shi's Life & Exile Route](assets/preview_journey_sushi_en.webp) --- ### Feature 4: Easter Egg · Map Pinpoint Challenge — What Imperial Court Rank Would You Earn? Think you know Chinese historical geography? Click **`Quiz ›`** in the corner of the **Universal Search Box** guide bar (or type `quiz` for **`Map Pinpoint · Ancient Place Quiz`**): - **Dynastic Historical Clues + Blind Map Pinpointing**: City labels are hidden while the prompt asks you to locate an ancient city across a 10-round progressive difficulty deck—accompanied by **dynastic historical clues** (without spoiling the modern city name). Drop your pin to preview and adjust, click the on-pin **`✓ Confirm`** button to lock in your answer with concentric distance score rings, and earn points based on great-circle distance to the true coordinates! - Complete 10 rounds to receive a traditional imperial cartographic title such as **Grand Historian & Master Cartographer (太史令 · 舆图大家)**, **Director of the Bureau of Operations (职方郎中)**, or **Prefectural Retainer (州郡从事)**. > [Try It Live: Western Han Emperor Wu, Yuanshou 2 (121 BCE) · Start the Map Pinpoint Challenge →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en) ![Western Han 121 BCE · Map Pinpoint Challenge Preview](assets/preview_quiz_challenge_en.webp) --- ## Keyboard Shortcuts & Shareable Deep Links ### Keyboard Shortcuts | Key / Action | Effect | | :--- | :--- | | **`/`** or **`Cmd/Ctrl + K`** | Focus the **Universal Search Box**: search **historical figures** (`Qin Shi Huang`/`Zhang Qian`/`Su Shi`), **ancient & modern cities** (`Xianyang`/`Chang'an`/`Luoyang`/`Kaifeng`), **reigning monarchs** (`Emperor Wu of Han`/`Taizong of Tang`/`Liu Che`/`Li Shimin`), **imperial eras** (`Zhenguan`/`Yongle`/`Kangxi`), **poetic & battlefield landmarks** (`Red Cliffs`/`Wuzhang Plains`/`Languan`/`Lanting`), **mountain passes** (`Hangu Pass`/`Jianmen Pass`/`Yumen Pass`), **historical events**, or the **Ancient Place Quiz** | | **`←` / `→`** or bottom **`‹ / ›`** | Jump to the previous / next historical phase, milestone event, or person event stop (hold `Shift + ← / →` to step by `10` years) | | **`Space`** | Auto-play / pause timeline evolution (or auto-advance stops in Person Chronicle mode) | | **`Esc`** | Close active popups/cards, clear search highlights, or exit custom multi-stop routes | | **`Single-click city` / `Double-click map`** | Open the 18-era **Trace Place & Key Events** genealogy card for that location | | **`Hover / Click legend swatch`** | Hover to isolate & highlight that polity's territory; click to auto-zoom to its bounding box | ### Shareable Deep Links Append query parameters to share any historical moment, battle, city genealogy, or multi-stop route: - **Jump to a specific year or territorial shift**: [`?year=-403&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-403&lang=en) (403 BCE · Partition of Jin) / [`?year=-121&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&lang=en) (121 BCE · Huo Qubing opens the Hexi Corridor) / [`?year=648&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=648&lang=en) (648 CE · Four Garrisons of Anxi & Wang Xuance in India) / [`?year=1288&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1288&lang=en) (1288 CE · Yuan Xuanzhengyuan over Tibet) / [`?year=1881&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1881&lang=en) (1881 CE · Zeng Jize recovers Ili) / [`?year=1945&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1945&lang=en) (1945 CE · Retrocession of Taiwan) - **Pinpoint a famous battle**: [`?year=-260&place=长平&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-260&place=长平&lang=en) (Battle of Changping) / [`?year=208&place=赤壁&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=208&place=赤壁&lang=en) (Battle of Red Cliffs) / [`?year=383&place=淝水&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=383&place=淝水&lang=en) (Battle of Fei River) - **Inspect a city's 2,400-year genealogy**: [`?year=741&place=长安&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=741&place=长安&lang=en) (Chang'an / Xi'an) / [`?year=1415&place=应天府&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1415&place=应天府&lang=en) (Jiankang / Yingtian / Nanjing) / [`?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en) (Han Yu at Languan Pass) - **Plot a custom poetic or campaign route**: [`?year=763&place=剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=763&place=剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳&lang=en) (Du Fu's 763 CE homeward route) / [`?year=1079,1080,1094,1097&place=湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1079,1080,1094,1097&place=湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州&lang=en) (Su Shi's multi-year exile route across Huzhou, Huangzhou, Huizhou, and Danzhou) - **Open a person's spatio-temporal chronicle**: [`?person=qinshihuang&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=qinshihuang&lang=en) (Qin Shi Huang) / [`?person=zhangqian&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=zhangqian&lang=en) (Zhang Qian) / [`?person=zhugeliang&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=zhugeliang&lang=en) (Zhuge Liang) / [`?person=xuanzang&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=xuanzang&lang=en) (Xuanzang) / [`?person=libai&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=libai&lang=en) (Li Bai) / [`?person=sushi&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=sushi&lang=en) (Su Shi) / [`?person=wangyangming&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=wangyangming&lang=en) (Wang Yangming) - **Compare several people or follow an event**: [`?person=libai,dufu&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=libai,dufu&lang=en) (Li Bai & Du Fu) / [`?person=caocao,liubei,sunquan&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=caocao,liubei,sunquan&lang=en) (Cao Cao, Liu Bei & Sun Quan) / [`?event=anshi&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?event=anshi&lang=en) (An Lushan Rebellion) - **Start a quiz round**: [`?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en) (Map Pinpoint Challenge) - **Switch UI language**: [`?lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en) (English) / [`?lang=zh-tw`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=zh-tw) (Traditional Chinese) / [`/`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/) (Simplified Chinese) ### Embed in Your Page Put any view of the atlas into a blog post, Notion page, or course site: 1. Open the atlas and set up the view you want (a year, a regime profile, a place card, or a person's trajectory). The address bar always mirrors what you see. 2. Copy the URL and add `&embed=1`. 3. Paste it into an ` ``` The embedded map hides the site chrome and keeps only the map, a compact timeline, a title chip, an "Open in Jiangshan Atlas ↗" link, and a note that historical borders are approximate. Readers click once to start panning and zooming, so scrolling your page never gets stuck on the map. | Parameter | Effect | |---|---| | `embed=1` | Turn on embed mode (required) | | `year`, `polity`, `person`, `stop`, `trace`, `lang` | Same as the share links above | | `from=1072&to=1126` | Limit the timeline to this range; the timeline zooms to show only it | | `lock=1` | Freeze the map at `year` and hide the timeline | | `autoplay=1` | Play a person's trajectory stop by stop (with `person`), or play the timeline | WeChat Official Accounts, Zhihu, and Xiaohongshu do not allow iframes; share the plain link there instead. --- ## AI Agent, MCP & LLM Integration **Chronicles of the Realm** works out of the box as a **historical-geography visualization engine for LLMs, MCP Clients, and AI Agents**. Models **never need to guess latitude/longitude coordinates**—simply extract two semantic parameters from a poem or historical text, **`year`** and **`place`**, and the atlas automatically resolves ancient/modern place names, centers the camera, renders dynastic borders and multi-stop trajectories, and opens the **Trace Place** genealogy card: - **Machine-Readable Specification**: [`llms.txt`](llms.txt) - **Zero-Dependency Local MCP Server (`stdio`)**: [`scripts/mcp_server.js`](scripts/mcp_server.js) — add to Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, or Gemini CLI `mcpServers`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "jiangshan-atlas": { "command": "node", "args": ["/absolute/path/to/jiangshan-map/scripts/mcp_server.js"] } } } ``` Exposes 3 native MCP tools (`<5ms` offline response, zero npm dependencies): - `inspect_place({ year, place, lang? })`: Returns reigning monarch/era, controlling regime (`polity`), macro-region (`dao/lu/province`), prefecture (`jun/zhou/fu`), modern province/city, 2,400-year `lore`, and shareable deep-link URL. - `inspect_person({ person, stop?, lang? })`: Returns a historical figure or monarch's biography, chronological geocoded stops across dynasties, and shareable deep-link URL. - `search_atlas({ query, limit?, lang? })`: Searches across all ancient cities, poetic & battlefield landmarks, mountain passes, historical figures, imperial eras, and chronological milestones. - **Ready-to-Use Agent Skill**: [`skills/jiangshan-atlas/SKILL.md`](skills/jiangshan-atlas/SKILL.md) (includes the zero-dependency CLI renderer [`skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py`](skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py)) ```bash # Install into Claude Code / Gemini / Jetski global skills directory: mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills ~/.gemini/config/skills && cp -r skills/jiangshan-atlas ~/.claude/skills/ && cp -r skills/jiangshan-atlas ~/.gemini/config/skills/ ``` ### 1. Zero-Coordinate Dual-Parameter URL Protocol (0D Pinpoint / 1D Same-Year Route / 4D Multi-Year Route) | Mode | Example URL | Automatic Rendering Behavior | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Single-Point Pinpoint (0D)** | [`?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en)
*(Han Yu's 819 CE exile poem at Languan Pass)* | Jumps to Tang Yuanhe 14 (819 CE), drops a pin on Languan Pass in the Qinling Mountains, and opens its 2,400-year administrative genealogy card | | **Same-Year Multi-Stop Route (1D)** | [`?year=763&place=剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=763&place=剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳&lang=en)
*(Du Fu's 763 CE poem on recapturing Henan & Hebei)* | Plots numbered vermilion arcs `1` → `5` across the 763 CE Tang map and auto-fits the viewport; click any stop to inspect its genealogy | | **Multi-Year Space-Time Route (4D)** | [`?year=1079,1080,1094,1097&place=湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1079,1080,1094,1097&place=湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州&lang=en)
*(Su Shi's career across Huzhou, Huangzhou, Huizhou & Danzhou)* | Pairs `year[i]` with `place[i]`, labeling stops with their historical years and switching the underlying dynastic map whenever you click a stop | ### 2. CLI One-Command Screenshot & JSON Lookup (for Agent Tool Calls) ```bash # Single-point poetic landmark screenshot python3 skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py --year 819 --place 蓝关 --out /tmp/languan_819.png # Same-year multi-stop trajectory screenshot python3 skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py --year 763 --place 剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳 --out /tmp/dufu_763.png # Multi-year space-time trajectory screenshot python3 skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py --year 1079,1080,1094,1097 --place 湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州 --out /tmp/sushi_exile.png ``` ### 3. Browser JavaScript API (`window.atlasAPI`) & In-Browser WebMCP (`navigator.modelContext`) In browser automation environments (Playwright) or WebMCP-enabled AI browsers (`navigator.modelContext`), the page automatically registers `jiangshan_locate`, `jiangshan_inspect`, and `jiangshan_open_person`, and exposes `window.atlasAPI`: - `window.atlasAPI.locate({ year, place, zoom? })`: Drives the map to a single location or multi-stop trajectory and returns structured historical-geographic metadata. - `window.atlasAPI.inspect({ year, place, person?, stop? })`: Read-only query returning the controlling polity, ancient prefecture, modern province/city, leg distances, person events, and canonical shareable URL. - `window.atlasAPI.resolvePlace(place, year?)`: Resolves ancient and modern names for cities, strategic passes, poetic landmarks, and battlefields. - `window.atlasAPI.openPerson(person, stop?)` & `window.atlasAPI.search(query)`: Opens a person chronicle on the map or searches across the entire atlas. --- ## Run Locally No dependencies or build steps required. Clone and serve with any static HTTP server: ```bash git clone https://github.com/DeanChensj/jiangshan-map.git cd jiangshan-map python3 -m http.server 8000 ``` Then open `http://localhost:8000` in your browser. ## Run with Docker No local dependency needed. Build and start with Docker Compose: ```bash docker compose up -d --build ``` Then open `http://localhost:8008` (the port mapping `8008:80` is set in `docker-compose.yml`). The image is a plain `nginx:alpine` that serves this repository as static files: `Dockerfile` copies the working tree into `/usr/share/nginx/html`, and `.dockerignore` keeps the build context small by excluding `.git`, `.github`, `data/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`, `skills/`, Markdown files and `geojson/demo.html` — the site does not need any of them at runtime. To use another port, change the `ports` mapping in `docker-compose.yml` (e.g. `"9000:80"`) and run `docker compose up -d` again. After pulling upstream changes, rebuild with `docker compose up -d --build`. Without Compose: `docker build -t jiangshan-map:latest .` then `docker run -d -p 8008:80 --name jiangshan-map jiangshan-map:latest`. Note: the image is built locally; it is not published to any registry. --- ## GeoJSON Export (for Leaflet / MapLibre / QGIS) The app ships its geometry as compact topology-deduplicated VLQ bundles. To use the vector layers in other projects, generate standard RFC 7946 GeoJSON (EPSG:4326, lon/lat) locally; the output goes to `geojson/` and is not committed. The export covers 403 BCE to 1948; later years and the modern province layer are not included. The prefecture layer (郡 / 州 / 府) is left out by default because it derives from CHGIS, whose terms forbid redistribution; add `--with-prefectures` to include it for local academic, non-commercial use, and do not publish the result. ```bash node scripts/export_geojson.js # or: node scripts/export_geojson.js node scripts/export_geojson.js --with-prefectures # adds the CHGIS-derived prefecture layer (local academic use only) ``` - `snapshots/.geojson` — one file per territorial phase; each feature has a `bbox` and `layer` (`polity` / `region`, plus `prefecture` with `--with-prefectures`), `title`, `title_en`, `category`, `tint`, `anchor`. - `index.json` — every dynasty's phases with `from` / `to` years (negative = BCE, no year 0) and the matching snapshot file. - `corridors.geojson` (walls, canals, roads, sea routes), `settlements.geojson`, `milestones.geojson`, `neighbors.geojson`, and `modern/` (rivers, lakes, hydro labels; `appear` / `vanish` give the years historical river courses and lakes are shown). To look up a point without loading every phase, use [`geojson/jiangshan-locate.js`](geojson/jiangshan-locate.js): it loads `index.json` plus only the snapshot covering the year, then runs a bbox-filtered point-in-polygon test. ```js const atlas = JiangshanLocate.create(); // or create({ base: '' }) const hit = await atlas.locate(118.78, 32.06, 1415); // lon, lat, year hit.polity.properties.title; // 明 hit.region.properties.title; // 南直隶 hit.prefecture; // null unless exported with --with-prefectures (then 应天府) ``` After exporting, serve the repository (`python3 -m http.server 8000`) and open `http://localhost:8000/geojson/demo.html` for a Leaflet example: drag the year slider, click the map, or open `demo.html?year=1415&lon=118.78&lat=32.06` to load, highlight and zoom automatically. Historical borders are schematic approximations, not surveyed boundaries. The data is GPL-3.0 except the prefecture-level boundaries; see [Data Sources & License](#data-sources--license). --- ## Data Sources & License Code and the data created by this project are released under **GPL-3.0**. One layer is not: the prefecture-level boundaries derived from CHGIS, which stay under CHGIS's own terms. | Layer | Source | License | | :-- | :-- | :-- | | Code (app, scripts, CLI, MCP server) | This project | GPL-3.0 | | Polity outlines (`polity`) | Started from [aourednik/historical-basemaps](https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps) (GPL-3.0), then redrawn by hand against historical texts | GPL-3.0 | | First-level divisions (`region`: 刺史部 / 道 / 路 / 省 …) | Drawn by hand from historical texts; the source of early versions was not recorded | GPL-3.0 | | **Prefecture-level boundaries** (`prefecture`: 郡 / 州 / 府, incl. Warring States and Qin commanderies) | Derived from **CHGIS V6** and the **Robert M. Hartwell China Historical GIS**, simplified to 0.01° and edited by hand | **Not GPL-3.0.** Academic, non-commercial use only; do not redistribute. See below | | Settlements, milestones, journeys, person chronicles, place lore | Compiled by this project from historical texts | GPL-3.0 | | Modern provinces | DataV GeoAtlas (Alibaba Cloud) | Subject to DataV GeoAtlas terms | | Rivers, lakes, neighbouring countries | Public-domain data | Public domain | | Terrain hillshade | Rendered by `scripts/build_terrain_tiles.py` from [AWS Terrain Tiles](https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/) (public-domain **SRTM**, **GMTED2010**, **ETOPO1**); only shaded images at no finer than about 1 km per pixel are published | GPL-3.0 (images) | | Guqin audio | Wikimedia Commons (*Liu Shui*, *Pingsha Luoyan*, *Yangguan Sandie*, *Zuiyu Changwan*, *Jiu Kuang*) | Public domain | **Scholarly references (not data sources).** Boundaries are checked against historical texts and Tan Qixiang's *The Historical Atlas of China* (谭其骧主编《中国历史地图集》). No map images or data from that atlas are included in this repository. **Prefecture-level boundaries (CHGIS).** This layer is not covered by GPL-3.0 and is shown here for non-commercial, educational use. Do not republish it from this repository; if you need prefecture boundaries, download CHGIS from its official distribution (Harvard Dataverse) under its terms. `scripts/export_geojson.js` leaves this layer out unless run with `--with-prefectures`. Cite it as: *CHGIS, Version: 6. © Fairbank Center for Chinese Studies of Harvard University and the Center for Historical Geographical Studies at Fudan University, 2016.* Provenance details: [data/atlas/README.md](data/atlas/README.md). **Approximate boundaries.** Historical territories and administrative boundaries are schematic approximations of broad jurisdictions, not surveyed borders. Do not cite them as precise or authoritative. **Reusing this project.** For the GPL-3.0 layers, credit **江山时序 Jiangshan Atlas** with a link to https://github.com/DeanChensj/jiangshan-map and cite the upstream sources above. Screenshots that show the prefecture layer carry the CHGIS terms as well. **Rights holders.** If you hold rights in any material here and believe it is used improperly, please [open an issue](https://github.com/DeanChensj/jiangshan-map/issues); we will respond and remove it if needed. **Contributing**: see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) ([中文贡献指南](CONTRIBUTING_ZH.md)) for repository structure, data conventions, and validation checks. **Report a data error**: found a wrong year, place or description? [Open a data correction issue](https://github.com/DeanChensj/jiangshan-map/issues/new?template=data-error.yml) and cite a source if you can. Copyright © 2026 DeanChensj. repositories.name: cross-platform-llm-client
repositories.description: A unified cross-platform AI client supporting seamless transitions between standard cloud APIs and on-device, offline execution of custom and uncensored language models.
repositories.readme:
# PrivateLM

[![Live Web App](https://img.shields.io/badge/Live_Demo-Try_Web_App-02569B?style=for-the-badge&logo=flutter&logoColor=white)](https://ai-chat-orailnoor.web.app/)

A production-ready, cross-platform AI chat client built with Flutter. It unifies local on-device LLM inference (Android) with cloud API access, giving users full control over how their models run.

![Image generation tested on Moto G71 (Snapdragon), Oneplus 10r (Mediatek), Pixel 6A (Tensor), Poco F1 (Snapdragon), Samsung s23 (Snapdragon) 4 steps fast](PrivateLM.png)
_Image generation tested on Moto G71 (Snapdragon), Oneplus 10r (Mediatek), Pixel 6A (Tensor), Poco F1 (Snapdragon), Samsung s23 (Snapdragon) 4 steps fast_

![Generated on pixel 6 with 20 step](IMG_2390.png)
_Generated on pixel 6 with 20 step_

---

## What It Does

- **Local Inference on Android** — Download and run GGUF models directly on your phone using GPU-accelerated inference (Vulkan). No internet required after download.
- **Cloud API Fallback** — Seamlessly switch to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, or Kimi (Moonshot AI) when you need more power or are on unsupported platforms.
- **Multimodal Chat** — Send text and images in conversations. Vision support works with both local models (Qwen2-VL) and cloud providers.
- **Persistent Sessions** — All chats and settings are stored locally via Hive. Nothing leaves your device unless you explicitly choose cloud mode.
- **Background Services** — Firebase Cloud Messaging integration for push updates and background task handling.
- **Smart Auto-Configuration** — On first launch, the app detects your device's RAM and recommends optimal context size and token limits automatically.
- **Task Management (in development)** — A task view for structured, multi-step AI workflows is being built. It is not available in the app yet.

---

## Technical Architecture

### Stack

- **Framework:** Flutter 3.x (Dart >=3.3.0)
- **State Management:** GetX
- **Local Storage:** Hive
- **Networking:** Dio + `package:http`
- **Background Execution:** `flutter_background_service` + `flutter_local_notifications`
- **Push Notifications:** Firebase Core + Firebase Messaging

### Inference Pipeline

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        UI Layer                              │
│   ChatView / ModelView / ServerView / SettingsView          │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
                           │
┌──────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Controllers (GetX)                        │
│   ChatController · TaskController · ModelController         │
│   SettingsController · HomeController                       │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
                           │
┌──────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────┐
│                      Services                                │
│  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐ │
│  │ InferenceService│  │  CloudService   │  │DownloadSvc  │ │
│  │  (local GGUF)   │  │ (OpenAI/Claude/ │  │ (model dl)  │ │
│  │                 │  │  Gemini/Kimi)   │  │             │ │
│  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────┘ │
│  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐ │
│  │  HiveService    │  │ DeviceInfoSvc   │  │ExecutionSvc │ │
│  │  ( persistence) │  │  (RAM/GPU tier) │  │ (bg tasks)  │ │
│  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Local Inference (Android)

The app uses `llama_flutter_android`, a custom Flutter plugin wrapping `llama.cpp` for ARM64 devices. At runtime it:

1. **Detects GPU capabilities** via Vulkan to determine offload layers.
2. **Selects thread count** based on device tier (ultra / high / mid / low).
3. **Loads the GGUF model** with progress streaming.
4. **Generates tokens** via `generateChat()` with native chat-template support (ChatML, Llama-3, Gemma, Phi).
5. **Falls back** to manual prompt construction if native templates fail.

Idle detection (5s) and hard timeouts (180s) keep the UX responsive even on underpowered hardware.

### Cloud Inference

`CloudService` normalizes four different API shapes into a single interface:

- **OpenAI** — standard `/v1/chat/completions`
- **Anthropic** — Messages API with separate system param
- **Google Gemini** — `generateContent` with inline image base64
- **Kimi** — OpenAI-compatible endpoint from Moonshot AI

API keys are stored in Hive and never transmitted anywhere except to the provider's endpoint.

### Cross-Platform Abstraction

Local inference is conditionally compiled:

- **Android** → `inference_android.dart` (full llama.cpp engine)
- **Web** → `inference_stub.dart` (cloud-only, local coming soon)
- **iOS** → `inference_android.dart` (full llama.cpp engine via Metal GPU)

The `InferenceService` exposes `supportsLocalInference` so the UI can hide local-model UI on unsupported platforms.

---

## Supported Platforms

| Platform | Local Inference | Cloud APIs | Notes                           |
| -------- | --------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------- |
| Android  | ✅ Yes          | ✅ Yes     | CPU offload via NEON; minSdk 28 |
| iOS      | ✅ Yes          | ✅ Yes     | Metal GPU acceleration          |
| Web      | ❌ No           | ✅ Yes     | Cloud-only (local coming soon)  |

### iOS / iPad (Installation via AltServer)
The iOS/iPad release is distributed as a sideloadable IPA file. Due to the RAM requirements for local models, iPad is the recommended iOS target, but it can be installed on iPhones.

Here is how you can install the app using AltStore and AltServer:

**Prerequisites:**
* Ensure **AltServer** is installed and running on your Mac or Windows PC.
* Your iOS device must be connected to the same Wi-Fi network as your computer, or connected directly via a USB cable.
* You must have **AltStore** successfully installed on your iOS device.

**Installation Steps:**
1. **Download the IPA:** Go to the [Releases](https://github.com/orailnoor/cross-platform-llm-client/releases) page on your iOS device (using Safari) and download the latest `PrivateLM-iOS.zip` package, extract it to get the `.ipa` file.
2. **Open in AltStore:**
   * Locate the extracted `.ipa` file in your device's "Files" app.
   * Tap the **Share** button and select **AltStore** from the list of apps.
   * *Alternatively*, you can open the AltStore app, go to the **My Apps** tab, tap the **"+" (plus)** icon in the top-left corner, and select the downloaded IPA file.
3. **Install:** AltStore will begin installing the app. You may be prompted to enter your Apple ID credentials if this is your first time.
4. **Enable Developer Mode:** On iOS 16 and later, ensure "Developer Mode" is enabled in your device's Settings (`Settings > Privacy & Security > Developer Mode`) to launch the sideloaded app.
5. **Launch:** Once installation is finished, PrivateLM will appear in the **My Apps** tab in AltStore and on your device's home screen!

*Note: Sideloaded apps via AltStore expire after 7 days, but AltStore will attempt to automatically refresh them in the background when connected to the same Wi-Fi as your computer running AltServer.*

---

## Build Configuration

### Prerequisites

- Flutter SDK >=3.3.0
- Android SDK (API 26+)
- JDK 17
- NDK (bundled with Android SDK)

### Android

```bash
flutter pub get
flutter build apk --debug
```

Release APKs require a stable signing key. Copy
`android/key.properties.example` to `android/key.properties`, fill in the
keystore values, and keep both the key and its backup. Android accepts an APK
upgrade only when it is signed with the same key as the installed APK.

```bash
cp android/key.properties.example android/key.properties
flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi
```

Never rotate the signing key between GitHub releases. The per-ABI APKs must
also keep increasing the build number in `pubspec.yaml`.

### iOS

```bash
flutter pub get
cd ios
pod install
flutter build ios
```

### Web

```bash
flutter pub get
flutter build web --release
```

---

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE) for details.

repositories.readme:
The full full-stack framework for Rust

[![Crates.io][crates-badge]][crates-url] [![Docs.rs][docs-badge]][docs-url] [![MIT licensed][mit-badge]][mit-url] [![Build Status][actions-badge]][actions-url] [![Discord chat][discord-badge]][discord-url]
[crates-badge]: https://img.shields.io/crates/v/topcoat.svg?style=flat-square [crates-url]: https://crates.io/crates/topcoat [docs-badge]: https://img.shields.io/docsrs/topcoat?style=flat-square [docs-url]: https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat [mit-badge]: https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg?style=flat-square [mit-url]: https://github.com/tokio-rs/topcoat/blob/main/LICENSE [actions-badge]: https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/tokio-rs/topcoat/ci.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square [actions-url]: https://github.com/tokio-rs/topcoat/actions?query=workflow%3ACI+branch%3Amain [discord-badge]: https://img.shields.io/discord/500028886025895936.svg?logo=discord&style=flat-square [discord-url]: https://discord.gg/tokio Topcoat is a modular, batteries-included Rust framework for building full-stack apps. It prioritizes simplicity and productivity. See [Learn Topcoat](#learn-topcoat) to get started, or the [Roadmap](#roadmap) for what's coming next. **Early-stage and experimental. Expect breaking changes.** ```rust,ignore use topcoat::{ Result, context::Cx, router::{module_router, page}, view::{View, component, view}, }; #[tokio::main] async fn main() { topcoat::start(module_router!().build()).await.unwrap(); } #[page] async fn home(cx: &Cx) -> Result { Ok(view! { hello(name: "World") }) } #[component] async fn hello(cx: &Cx, name: &str) -> Result { Ok(view! {

"Hello, " (name) "!"

}) } ``` ## What makes Topcoat different ### Client reactivity without the boilerplate Topcoat renders all markup on the server: components can be async and query the database directly, eliminating all the traditional boilerplate needed for a separate API layer. Interactivity does not have to cost a round-trip, though. A `$(...)` expression is ordinary type-checked Rust that Topcoat evaluates on the server for the initial render and also translates to JavaScript, so it re-runs instantly in the browser. No wasm bundle, no client build step: ```rust,ignore #[component] async fn faq(cx: &Cx) -> Result { let open = signal(cx, || false); Ok(view! { // Runs entirely in the browser; no server round-trip.

"A full-stack Rust framework."

}) } ``` When an update does need the server, like fresh search results, mark the component as a `#[shard]`. Topcoat re-renders it on the server whenever one of its `$(...)` arguments changes and swaps the new HTML in place: ```rust,ignore #[component] async fn search(cx: &Cx) -> Result { let query = signal(cx, String::new); Ok(view! { // Updates as the user types. search_results(query: $(query.get())) }) } #[shard] async fn search_results(cx: &Cx, query: String) -> Result { Ok(view! {
    // Your own server-side code, like a database query: for product in search_products(cx, &query).await? {
  • (product.name)
    • }
}) } ``` ### Powerful, unsurprising HTML templates The `view!` macro stays true to HTML and Rust. Use familiar Rust control flow as part of your templates: ```rust,ignore view! {
for item in nav_items { (item.label) }
} ``` Use the `topcoat fmt` CLI command to automatically format `view!` snippets (and other macros) across your codebase. ### Module-based routing Topcoat can optionally infer your route tree from your app's module structure (without a build step): ```text src/ |-- app.rs -> / (and the root layout) `-- app/ |-- about.rs -> /about |-- _marketing.rs (layout, no URL segment) |-- _marketing/ | `-- pricing.rs -> /pricing |-- posts.rs -> /posts |-- posts/ | `-- id.rs -> /posts/{post_id} `-- api/ `-- health.rs -> GET /api/health ``` ### Premade components you can edit Topcoat UI is a component library based on [Tailwind](https://tailwindcss.com/) inspired by [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/). Components are copied into your project via the `topcoat ui` CLI command, meaning you can freely change their design and functionality to fit your use case: ```rust,ignore #[component] async fn delete_card(cx: &Cx) -> Result { Ok(view! { card( card_header( card_title("Delete workspace") card_description( "This permanently removes the workspace and all of its data." ) ) card_footer( attrs: attributes! { class="justify-end" }, button(variant: ButtonVariant::Ghost, "Cancel") button(variant: ButtonVariant::Destructive, "Delete workspace") ) ) }) } ``` ### Asset bundling The bundler scans your compiled binary for `asset!` calls, copies (or even downloads) every file into a local asset directory, and allows Topcoat to serve them efficiently with aggressive browser caching. ```rust,ignore const FERRIS: Asset = asset!("./ferris.png"); view! { } ``` Topcoat also ships with utilities for web fonts and icons, as well as easy integrations for [Fontsource](https://fontsource.org/) (Google Fonts) and [Iconify](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/). ### Built-in Tailwind support Enable the `tailwind` feature to integrate [Tailwind](https://tailwindcss.com/) into your project: ```rust,ignore view! { } ``` ## Learn Topcoat **Start here** - [Getting started](https://github.com/tokio-rs/topcoat/blob/main/docs/getting_started.md): create an app with `topcoat new` and run the dev server. - [Manual setup](https://github.com/tokio-rs/topcoat/blob/main/docs/manual_setup.md): add dependencies and wire up a minimal app yourself. - [Source code formatting](https://github.com/tokio-rs/topcoat/blob/main/docs/cli/fmt.md): `topcoat fmt` for macro bodies. **Rendering** - [`view!`](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/view/macro.view.html) mixes HTML, Rust expressions, control flow, and component calls. - [`#[component]`](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/view/attr.component.html) makes async functions callable from markup with named arguments and child content. - [`attributes!`](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/view/macro.attributes.html) collects attributes to pass through components and spread onto elements. - [`class!`](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/view/macro.class.html) joins base, optional, and conditional CSS classes. - [`suspense`](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/view/struct.suspense.html) shows a fallback while content loads. [`error_boundary`](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/view/struct.error_boundary.html) shows one if rendering fails. - [`live!` and `emit!`](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/view/macro.live.html) replace part of a page as async work produces new HTML. **Routing** - [Router](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/router/index.html): pages, layouts, and API routes; manual and auto-discovered. - [Module-based routing](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/router/macro.module_router.html): derive the route table from your module tree. - [Linking to handlers](https://github.com/tokio-rs/topcoat/blob/main/docs/router/href.md): use `href!` for navigation links, form actions, and redirects. **Working with requests** - [Context (`Cx`)](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/context/index.html): read request data and values stored by type. Add shared values with the router builder's `.with`, or use `cx.with` to add a value for part of a request. - [Memoization](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/context/attr.memoize.html): `#[memoize]` for per-request caching and fan-out dedup. - [Cookies](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/cookie/index.html): read and write the request cookie jar, with signed, encrypted, and prefixed cookies. - [Sessions](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/session/index.html): bring-your-own-storage session authentication: login/logout lifecycle, sliding expiration, and token rotation. **Asset system** - [Assets](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/asset/index.html): declare assets in Rust, serve them with content-hashed URLs. - [Fonts](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/font/index.html): bundle and serve web fonts. - [Icons](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/icon/index.html): download Iconify icon sets or declare your own. **Client reactivity** - [The runtime](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/runtime/index.html): signals, `$(...)` expressions, `@` event handlers, and `:` bind attributes. - [Expressions](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/runtime/macro.expr.html): the dual Rust/JavaScript expression language and its vocabulary. - [Procedures](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/runtime/attr.procedure.html): async server functions callable from the browser. - [Shards](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/runtime/attr.shard.html): components that re-render on the server when their arguments change. - [Client-side navigation](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/runtime/struct.link.html): links, prefetching, and navigation without a full document reload. **Miscellaneous** - [Topcoat UI](https://github.com/tokio-rs/topcoat/blob/main/docs/ui.md): premade components vendored into your project for you to edit. - [Metadata](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/metadata/index.html): titles, descriptions, and link previews for search engines and social networks, set per layout and page. - [Localization](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/l10n/index.html): choose the language for each request and display translations from Fluent files. - [Mail](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/mail/index.html): build mail with `Mail::builder`, deliver through SMTP, file, or in-memory transports. - [OpenAPI](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/openapi/index.html): describe API routes where they are declared and generate an OpenAPI document from the router. **Third-party integrations** - [Tailwind](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/tailwind/index.html): Tailwind CSS without Node, wired into the asset pipeline. - [htmx](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/htmx/index.html): drive partial HTML swaps from the server with request/response header helpers. - [Alpine AJAX](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/alpine_ajax/index.html): drive partial HTML swaps from the server with Alpine AJAX's request-header conventions. - [Datastar](https://docs.rs/topcoat/latest/topcoat/datastar/index.html): patch elements and signals into the page over server-sent events. ## Roadmap Planned features we'd like to bring to Topcoat. Have an idea? [Open an issue](https://github.com/tokio-rs/topcoat/issues). - [ ] Static export - [ ] (More) reactivity (`topcoat-runtime`) - [ ] More Topcoat UI components, full "blocks" e.g. sign-in form - [ ] Better [Toasty](https://github.com/tokio-rs/toasty) integration (safely create/update records from forms without listing out all the fields) - [ ] Validations - [ ] Docs for how to deploy Topcoat - [ ] Pre-rendering for static pages - [ ] `WebTransport` - [ ] Image optimization / resizing - [ ] Markdown support - [ ] Easier-to-use middlewares like rate-limiting - [ ] Authentication - [ ] Background jobs - [ ] Islands

repositories.name: ohmygame
repositories.description: The open-source studio for making games with AI. Your own one-person game studio. Everything you need to make games with AI, in one app. Game canvas.  Bring your own key.
repositories.readme:
**Your own one-person game studio.** Everything you need to make games with AI, in one app. **Make a game. Ship it everywhere. Earn from it.**

English · 简体中文

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d5805fe-92a2-40b4-a232-c7452f9a796a
> [!NOTE] > 🚧 OhMyGame is in beta. Expect rough edges. Join us and let's build it together! ## News - **2026-10 · beta 5** ([release notes](https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/releases/tag/v0.0.0-beta.5.0)) - **Now with interactive stories:** make visual novels, interactive films, and story games. Every screen is a web page the agent builds from your description, with video, dialogue, choices, or even a mini-game, so your story isn't limited to fixed node types. - **Bring your own agent:** Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode can run the conversation, or you can bring OhMyGame to them. - **Plugins:** build in Godot, Unity, Unreal Engine, or Cocos Creator; make assets in Blender, Aseprite, or Tiled; ship to WeChat Mini Games, Douyin Mini Games, or TapTap, and [earn from your game](#-publish-and-earn-one-link-or-the-platforms-where-players-pay). ## What it is Making a game takes design docs, 2D art, 3D models, video, code, and somewhere to put it when it's done. Today those live in five or six different tools. OhMyGame puts them in one app: describe your game, and the agent designs it, makes the assets, builds it, plays it to check it works, and publishes it to a link you can share. Two core design ideas shape it: 1. **Everything lives on a canvas.** Design docs, concept art, 3D models, and video sit side by side on one board. One character sketch can grow into more art, a video, or a rigged 3D model, and everything is ready to use in your game. 2. **The agent does the work.** It drives the canvas the way you would: drafting the design doc, turning a character sketch into a rigged 3D model, writing the code, and playtesting the result. It's open source and works with 40+ model providers through Pi, from Anthropic and OpenAI to DeepSeek and Qwen. Your keys stay on your machine, there are no per-run credits, and what you make is yours. ## Features ### 🤖 Agent: drives the canvas, builds and plays the game The agent works the canvas the way you would: it drafts the design doc, lays out boards, and generates assets on them. It reads the design doc, writes the code, and runs the game in a live preview. Then it opens the game in a window you can watch and plays it, including real-time canvas and WebGL games. When it finds a problem, it tries a fix and plays again. Along the way it can generate images, video, 3D models, and audio, search the web, and use MCP servers and plugins. **▶ The agent playtesting a new item feature on desktop and mobile, then reporting what it found (sped up 4×).** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3cb982e8-a4a8-4715-bf3c-df4e41e7855b ### 🎨 Canvas: design docs, art, video, 3D, and audio on one board Every game project has a design space: a main design doc plus boards where the doc, images, video, 3D models, and audio sit side by side. Nodes can use each other as references, so one character design can lead to more images, a video, a voice line, or a rigged and animated 3D model. Results go into a shared Asset Library that your games can use. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5a35964d-87b3-4153-8b1b-fc6deced5bb3 ### 🔗 Publish and earn: one link, or the platforms where players pay Sign in and publish: OhMyGame builds your game and gives it a link anyone can play in the browser. Republishing updates the same link. Published games are listed in the in-app Community, where you can play what others have made, sort by latest, most viewed, or most liked, visit creators' profiles, and like the games you enjoy. A one-person studio should pay for itself. Beyond the Community, plugins take your game to the platforms where players pay. | Ship to | Earn from | How | | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- | | WeChat Mini Games, Douyin Mini Games | Ads, in-app purchases | [Platform plugins](#-plugins-connect-with-more-game-dev-tools) | | TapTap | Downloads, in-app purchases | TapTap Maker plugin | | Steam and other stores | Sales | Export from Godot or Unity with their plugins | | itch.io, Poki, CrazyGames | Sales, ad revenue share | Upload your Web Game build | **Your game, your revenue.** OhMyGame takes no cut of what your game earns. ### 🧑‍💻 Bring your own agent Already use Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode? Choose it in the model picker and it runs the conversation with its own sign-in. It gets the whole studio: the canvas, media generation, playtesting, plugins, and Undo, with your history kept in OhMyGame. See [coding agents](docs/coding-agents.md). ### 🔌 Use OhMyGame from Claude Code, Codex, and other agents Already working in another coding agent? Turn on **Settings → MCP Server** and add OhMyGame to Claude Code or Codex with the command shown there. They get OhMyGame's media generation with your providers, the canvas, and playtesting, plus a Skill that explains the workflow. DeepSeek Harness and other MCP clients can add the `ohmygame-studio` command shown there. See [External agents](docs/external-agents.md). ### 🧩 Plugins: connect with more game dev tools Plugins let the agent work in the engines and tools you already know: - **Engines:** Godot, Unity, Unreal Engine, and Cocos Creator. - **Platforms:** TapTap Maker, WeChat Mini Games, and Douyin Mini Games. - **Assets:** Blender, Aseprite, and Tiled. Turn them on in **Plugins**, or build your own with Plugin Builder. Engine plugins use each engine's own editor and tools, so install those first. See [Plugins](docs/plugins.md). ## What you can make Three games our team made with OhMyGame:
Interactive film Island builder Deckbuilding roguelike
### 🎮 Web games **The best place to start.** 2D and 3D games for the browser, built with Three.js, React Three Fiber, or Phaser. The agent follows a complete web game workflow: a design doc, key-screen mockups, production art, a playable core loop, and playtesting in the live preview. Games fit any window size, support touch, and publish to a shareable link. The project is a normal web project you can open in any editor. ### 🎬 Interactive stories Interactive films, visual novels, and story games. Each screen is a free web page with its own images, video, and code: a main menu, a case archive, a dialogue, a puzzle. You connect them on a graph, and the runtime handles state, saves, music, and navigation. The story plays as its own web page, and the runtime is part of the project, so the agent can change anything about how it plays. The architecture and authoring model are documented in [Playable Nodes](docs/playable-nodes/README.md). ### 🎲 General games: any engine or stack **General Game** doesn't assume an engine or stack. Start from an idea, bring a project in any engine, or make tools and content for your game. The Game Studio plugin coordinates design, production art, implementation, and verification across engines, and the [engine plugins](#-plugins-connect-with-more-game-dev-tools) work in the engine you use. For Godot, start a **Godot** project from the sidebar. When the output is a web page, preview, playtesting, and publishing work as they do for Web games; native games use their engine's own tools. See [General Game details](docs/runtime.md#agent-game-use). **Making a browser game? Choose Web Game**: it is tuned for the browser. ## How it's built The idea that holds this together: one agent drives every part of the studio. **1 · A full Pi agent with a GUI.** OhMyGame runs [Pi](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent) with its full toolset and persistent sessions, in a GUI built for watching results rather than reading diffs. Close the app, come back, and the project, conversation, and context are still there. You describe, review, and steer; editing by hand is always possible, but it is not the main path. **2 · Every workspace is files.** A web game is a normal web project. A design doc is Markdown, and boards and the Asset Canvas share one JSON node model. An interactive story is a node graph on disk. Each comes with an `AGENTS.md` and JSON schemas, so the agent edits them the same way it edits code, and the visual editors read and write the same files. **3 · Games are tool calls.** Playing the game (`game_use`), generating media, and checking story nodes are ordinary Pi tools, next to its coding tools. That is why the agent can chain them: draft a design, make the art, write the code, and play the result in one conversation. ## Any model, your keys OhMyGame does not lock you into one model or charge per run. - **Coding models from 40+ providers** through Pi, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM, MiniMax, xAI, Mistral, Groq, OpenRouter, Amazon Bedrock, and Vercel AI Gateway. - **Sign in with a subscription you already have**, such as ChatGPT Plus/Pro or GitHub Copilot, or paste an API key. - **Coding agents you already use**: Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode run a conversation with their own sign-in, while OhMyGame keeps its history, Undo, canvas, media tools, and plugins. Enable them in Settings; native CLI permission limits apply. See [coding agents](docs/coding-agents.md). - **Media models** for images, video, 3D, and audio through OpenAI, Codex, OpenRouter, Volcengine Ark / BytePlus ModelArk, MiniMax, Meshy, Tripo, Hyper3D, and Doubao Speech / Seed Audio. - **Custom providers and model aliases** with selectable language, image, video and 3D uses, protocol templates and generation defaults. See [custom model configuration](docs/custom-models.md). Keys stay in the local daemon. They never reach the agent's workspace, your game, or the renderer. ## Quick start ### Download Grab the installer from the buttons at the top or from [Releases](https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/releases). Builds are available for macOS (Apple silicon) and Windows (x64). The Windows build is not code-signed yet, so Windows may show a SmartScreen warning during install. See [the changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for changes in each release, or open **Settings → About → Changelog** inside the app. ### First run ![First-run AI connection screen](docs/assets/first-run-onboarding.png) OhMyGame ships without a model. On first launch, it walks you through setup: 1. **Get started.** Language and appearance follow your system; change them anytime in Settings. 2. **Choose your AI.** Use the built-in OhMyGame agent with a model provider (sign in or paste an API key), or a Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode CLI you already have. Use **+** to add a custom or local endpoint. **Skip this step** moves on without a model. A language model alone can design and build a game. Generating media needs a corresponding provider, which you connect in **Settings → Providers**: | To make | Connect | | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Design docs, code, playtests | Any language model provider | | Images and sprites | Codex CLI (local sign-in), OpenAI (API key), OpenRouter, or Volcengine Ark / BytePlus ModelArk | | Video | OpenRouter, Volcengine Ark / BytePlus ModelArk, or MiniMax | | 3D models, rigging, animation | Meshy, Tripo, or Hyper3D (capabilities vary by provider) | | Voice, sound effects, music | Doubao Speech and Seed Audio (Volcengine) | ChatGPT sign-in doesn't cover OpenAI's image API; add a separate API key in the OpenAI provider's **Image models** section. The **Codex CLI** image provider uses your local Codex sign-in instead. See [OpenAI image connections](docs/custom-models.md#openai-image-connections). 3. **Choose where to start:** describe a game in the prompt box on the home screen, start a blank project, or import a folder you already have. Web search works without setup. Making games locally needs no account; sign in only to publish. Reopen this setup from **Settings → About → View getting started**. ### Run from source Requires Bun 1.4.2 or newer for the toolchain and Node.js 22.19+ for the daemon. ```bash git clone --branch main https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame.git cd ohmygame bun install --frozen-lockfile bun run dev # web renderer + local daemon # or bun run dev:desktop # Electron app ``` This uses the release branch. For development contributions, start from `dev` using [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#fork-and-create-a-branch). Local development can start without cloud configuration; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#configuration) for optional integrations. ## Privacy Your projects and keys stay on your machine. Prompts and generation requests go directly to the model providers you choose. Publishing requires an OhMyGame account and uploads only your game's static build. Release builds check for updates and send usage data and crash reports. Usage data is linked to your account when you sign in, and you can turn it off in **Settings → About**. Builds from source send no telemetry. The desktop app keeps redacted logs on your machine; they leave it only if you export them from **Settings → About → Diagnostics** and share the file. See [logs and diagnostics](docs/diagnostics.md). ## Roadmap We're working on plain-language playtest reports, remixing games from the Community, and Intel Mac / Linux builds. See [Issues](https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/issues) for what's next, and vote with 👍 on what matters to you. Want to help? Look for [`help wanted`](https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/labels/help%20wanted) issues. ## Contributing Issues and PRs are welcome. Start contribution branches from `dev` and target ordinary PRs at `dev`; `main` receives releases. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for setup, checks, and review, [中文快速指引](docs/contributing.zh-CN.md) for a short Chinese introduction, and [the documentation index](docs/README.md) for module guides. Report security issues using [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Star History ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE). The OhMyGame name and logo are not covered by the license.

repositories.name: vorssaint-utils
repositories.description: Free and open-source macOS menu bar toolkit.
repositories.readme:
Vorssaint

One menu bar icon doing the job of a dozen paid Mac apps.
Install only what you use.

Website · Install · Features · Privacy · Changelog · Contact · Discord

For anything private, email hello@vorssaint.com.

Sponsors

Help keep Vorssaint free and open source. Share your product with Mac users.


Your product here
Your logo · Your name · Your link

Become our first sponsor →

Per app volume, a real system monitor, a better app switcher, window snapping, Dock previews, clipboard history, text snippets, a file shelf, an uninstaller. The utilities Mac users usually buy one by one, together behind a single menu bar icon, with no account, no telemetry and no subscription. ## Install only what you use Choose individual features or start with a preset. Uninstalled features stop loading and disappear from the interface; reinstalling restores their settings. Setup asks only for the permissions your choices need.

Reorder or hide panel sections, choose a compact layout, and export settings to another Mac or [keep them in your dotfiles](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#keeping-settings-in-your-dotfiles). The app supports more than a dozen languages. ## Everything it does ### Sound - **Volume mixer.** Set volume per app, boost quiet audio past 100%, and pin or reorder favorites. No audio driver required. - **Per app output.** Play music through speakers while a call uses your headset. - **Output switcher.** Switch audio outputs with a shortcut and lower the volume when headphones disconnect. - **Microphone tools.** Choose a preferred input, adjust its level on supported devices, and apply available microphone mute or input-volume controls with one shortcut. Siri and some apps may still hear you; Mic Mute is not a privacy lock. Its indicator shows that the feature is on, not that every app receives silence. - **Music app blocker.** Prevent unwanted Music launches after detected playback-button presses. Requires Accessibility. ### Know what your Mac is doing - **System monitor.** CPU, GPU, memory, temperatures, battery health and power use, with history graphs and a view of energy-hungry apps. - **Fan Control (beta).** Set manual fan speeds or temperature curves and monitor live RPM. - **Menu bar readouts.** Put your chosen readings, usage bars, battery time or fan speed directly in the menu bar. - **Network.** See live traffic, session totals and your local IP address, or run a speed test. - **Alerts.** Get notified about sustained CPU load, high temperatures, memory pressure, low disk space or low battery. ### Windows and the Dock - **App switcher.** Switch between apps and windows with live previews, search and display filters. A simpler mode works without screen capture. - **Window layout.** Snap windows into layouts, move them between displays and restore earlier positions using shortcuts, screen edges or modifier-drag gestures. - **Dock Preview.** Hover over Dock icons to preview windows across desktops. Switch, close, move or snap them from the preview. - **Dock clicks.** Click an active app's Dock icon to minimize, hide or cycle through its windows. - **Maximize windows.** Use the green button to fill the screen without creating another Space. - **Fixed Space order.** Keep Spaces in the order you set instead of rearranging them by recent use. Turning it off restores your previous setting. - **Quit on close.** Quit selected apps when their last window closes. - **Quit and close protection.** Prevent accidental ⌘Q or ⌘W with a hold, double press or extra modifier, per app.

### Keyboard and mouse - **Text snippets.** Expand short triggers into text with clipboard, date and time variables, or insert snippets from a searchable menu. - **Smooth scrolling.** Give your mouse wheel a fluid glide with adjustable speed and response. - **Pointer acceleration.** Disable mouse acceleration and restore your previous setting when turned off. - **Linear scrolling.** Make every mouse wheel notch scroll the same number of lines, however fast the wheel spins. - **Focus follows mouse.** Bring the window under the pointer forward after an adjustable pause. - **Scroll direction.** Invert vertical and horizontal mouse scrolling independently of the trackpad. - **Scroll sideways while holding a key.** Turn vertical wheel movement into horizontal scrolling while holding a chosen key. - **Side buttons.** Use mouse Back and Forward buttons in Finder, browsers and compatible apps. - **Mouse button shortcuts.** Assign keys to extra buttons and side wheels, or use button-drag gestures for Spaces and Mission Control. - **Middle click.** Turn a three-finger trackpad press into a middle click. - **Apps to leave alone.** Exclude chosen apps from mouse enhancements. - **Extra click filter.** Ignore accidental rapid clicks from worn mouse buttons without delaying normal clicks. - **Key debounce.** Filter repeated letters caused by a worn keyboard. - **Super key.** Use Caps Lock or a right-side modifier as a shortcut combination, with a separate tap action and app exclusions. - **Keyboard shortcuts.** Manage feature shortcuts in one place, including optional takeover of supported macOS shortcuts while a feature is active. ### Clipboard, files and links - **Clipboard history.** Search local text, image and file history, pin favorites, preview entries and paste with shortcuts. - **Auto clear clipboard.** Clear the system clipboard after a delay, sleep or lock, while keeping saved history. - **Paste as plain text.** Paste without formatting while preserving the original clipboard content. - **Shelf.** Park files, text and links near your cursor while dragging, then drop or share them later. - **Finder shortcuts.** Move files with ⌘X and ⌘V, rename with F2, or paste copied images as PNG files. - **Clean URL.** Remove tracking parameters from links, manually or automatically. - **Disk image installer.** Install an app from a mounted disk image and eject it, with optional download cleanup. ### Everyday tools - **Dynamic Island.** Keep music, notifications, calendars, timers, downloads and everyday controls around the camera cutout, or a simulated one on other Macs. Customize sections and shortcuts, with optional lyrics, a live equalizer, camera preview and file tools. - **AI agents.** Follow Claude, Codex, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot in the Dynamic Island: plan limits and when they reset where available, tokens, API value, models, projects and live work, with a notice when a long task finishes. Codex's banked resets can be used from there too, and each extra Codex account (`CODEX_HOME`) can have a limits card of its own. Copilot uses local CLI/app session logs; its token totals update when shutdown metrics arrive, and aggregate API-value estimates use base rates. - **Command Bar.** Search apps, windows, files, clipboard history, snippets and app menu commands from one field. Calculate, convert units, find emoji or run saved scripts. - **Quick panel.** Open a floating palette of favorite tools with ⌃⌘V. - **Quick toggles.** Switch appearance, hide desktop icons, eject disks, empty the Trash, lock the screen and more. - **Quit apps.** See every open app in one list and quit them one by one, all at once or all but the one in front. - **Radial menu.** Open a customizable wheel of apps, files, shortcuts and tools around the pointer, with profiles and submenus. - **Scratchpad.** Keep autosaved notes in tabs, with Markdown preview and export, in a floating window or Dynamic Island. - **Cleaning Mode.** Lock keyboard input while cleaning, with a black screen or a small visible indicator. ### Capture and create - **Screen capture.** Switch between screenshots, recording, text recognition and color picking in one selector with a pixel magnifier. - **Screenshot.** Capture an area, window, screen or scrolling page. Annotate, crop, redact, add backgrounds and watermarks, pin captures, send them through the Share menu or share an expiring link. - **Screen recording.** Record with separate system-audio and microphone tracks. Trim, cut, add automatic zooms, blur private details and export video or GIFs, or share an expiring link. - **Camera preview.** Check your camera in a floating mirror or Dynamic Island before a call. - **Copy text from screen.** Recognize text offline from any screen area, or read a QR code. - **Color picker.** Copy a screen color as HEX, RGB, HSL or SwiftUI code. - **Media tools.** Compress and edit videos, batch-convert images, add watermarks, make GIFs and extract text, all locally. ### App management - **App updates.** Check store apps, package-managed apps and supported developer feeds in one list. Install managed updates together or open an app's own updater. - **Cleaner.** Remove caches, logs and app leftovers, manually or on a schedule. - **Messaging downloads.** Review, organize or move messaging downloads to the Trash using retention rules. - **Uninstaller.** Remove apps and review their related caches, preferences and helpers before moving them to the Trash. - **Homebrew manager.** Search, install and remove formulae and casks without opening a terminal. - **Port manager.** Find processes listening on network ports and stop them with Kill Process when installed. ### Energy and display - **Keep awake.** Keep your Mac working on a timer, with the lid closed, or while selected apps, power or external displays are present. - **Displays.** Control individual displays and brightness, with hardware control where supported, half or quarter steps for the brightness keys, optional extra dimming below a monitor's minimum, software dimming as a fallback, and the volume and mute of a monitor's built-in speakers. - **Extra brightness.** Use a MacBook Pro XDR display's HDR headroom to go beyond its normal maximum brightness. - **Bluetooth on sleep.** Disconnect Bluetooth during sleep and restore it on wake only if Vorssaint turned it off. ## Install With [Homebrew](https://brew.sh): ```sh brew install --cask vorssaint ``` Or grab the disk image from the [releases page](https://github.com/vorssaint/vorssaint-utils/releases) and drag Vorssaint into Applications. Builds are signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized, so macOS opens them without a fuss and your permissions survive updates. ## Uninstall With Homebrew: ```sh brew uninstall --cask vorssaint ``` To remove Vorssaint completely, including its settings and permissions: ```sh ./Tools/uninstall.sh ``` ## Private by default Vorssaint is local-first, with no account, analytics or tracking. The network is touched only by things you can see: update checks, the speed test, Homebrew actions, optional online lyric lookup, temporary screenshot or recording links and feedback you explicitly send. The full story is in the [privacy notes](docs/PRIVACY.md). Permissions get the same treatment. Every one is optional, the app explains each in plain words, shows which features actually use it, and even tells you when a permission you granted is no longer needed by anything, with a shortcut to revoke it.

See the [permissions guide](docs/PERMISSIONS.md) for which features need access and what remains available without it. ## What you need - A Mac with Apple Silicon - macOS 14 Sonoma or newer ### Build it yourself ```sh git clone https://github.com/vorssaint/vorssaint-utils.git cd vorssaint-utils ./build.sh --dev # build the separate Developer variant ./build.sh --dev --install # install and launch it ``` Xcode Command Line Tools are the only requirement. The [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) covers the layout and conventions. Official builds come only from the maintainer: the GPL covers the source, while the Vorssaint name, icon and look are covered by [TRADEMARKS.md](TRADEMARKS.md), so forks need their own identity. ## When something misbehaves See [troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) for launch problems, permissions and missing previews, or [support](SUPPORT.md) for help. ## Documentation - [Privacy](docs/PRIVACY.md), what does and does not leave your Mac - [Permissions](docs/PERMISSIONS.md), every macOS permission in plain words - [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md), the common fixes - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md), build, layout and conventions - [Support](SUPPORT.md), where to get help - [Security](SECURITY.md), how to report a vulnerability ## Community Vorssaint went from first commit to the front of GitHub trending in three days, top of the Swift charts, and issues and pull requests have shaped every release since. Bug reports, feature ideas and translations are all welcome, starting from the [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md). Vorssaint is free and will stay that way. If it earned its place in your menu bar, a star helps other people find it, and a [coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/vorssaint) keeps the maintainer awake, with or without the Keep awake feature. ## Acknowledgements - App icon designed by [@divisionseven](https://github.com/divisionseven) ## License [GPL 3.0 or later](LICENSE), copyright 2026 Vorssaint. The license covers the source code; the Vorssaint name, logo and look are covered separately in [TRADEMARKS.md](TRADEMARKS.md).
